note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative. Times are fictional labels. The context is supplied and changes only the surroundings of the same conversation; nothing is concluded from it automatically — no presumption, no intention to be bound, no binding force, validity or formation, no jurisdiction.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Fictional conversation: Party A offers to drive to the fair on Saturday, Party B offers to share the fuel cost; the messages cross between the parties and the supplied context — a social gathering — draws itself round the same conversation; nothing is concluded from it.

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: Substantive alternative: other parties and another conversation (repainting a hall), Party B's message sent first, and the supplied context a negotiation meeting (a table with a notepad on the badge); the conversation is unchanged by it and nothing is concluded from it.

offer.title: We could repaint the hall in May

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long names, captions, references, texts and labels, three terms, two annotations; the two receipts are supplied with one position (order to be examined); a long context description. Standing coordinator rule item 20 (caps with the true reason). The pre-cap values are kept in LAW-0465.presets.precap.json. Each capped field was restored alone to its pre-cap value on top of the shipped preset and rendered: the message title 34 -> 67 makes 9:16 and 1:1 fail (nofit: the strip and the cards no longer fit, the hands cannot reach); the three term values 12 -> 30, 10 -> 28 and 7 -> 34 each make 1:1 fail (nofit: the cards grow too tall for the racks); the two annotations 29 -> 38 and 17 -> 40 each find no place at 1:1. With every capped field restored, 9:16 and 1:1 fail. Every capped value stays longer than its baseline counterpart (title 34 vs 26, term values 12 vs 8 and 10 vs 3; the third term and the annotations have no baseline counterpart); every count is kept or larger (three terms, five events, two annotations). Shipped: 16.1 px text in each ratio; heads 84.7 px (16:9), 76.7 px (9:16), 60.3 px (1:1) (rendered).
